fields.expected:
Most of my recent work has been on ML systems that have to hold up in production, not just in a notebook. At Summer Atlantic Capital I own major parts of the ML core of an anomaly-detection system: the event-ingestion pipeline, temporal sequence models over event streams using RNN and Transformer-style approaches, anomaly scoring, a learning-to-rank layer for alert prioritization, and a versioned FastAPI microservice serving the detection API. The thing I kept coming back to there was that raw model performance was not the constraint. An anomaly system that fires too often just creates a second problem, so ranking quality, failure modes, and explanation quality mattered as much as the score itself.

I also care a lot about evaluation. At Intelehealth I designed an evaluation framework for LLM-generated clinical outputs against a 4,169-case clinical standard, using stratified sampling to surface systematic failure modes rather than a single aggregate number. That shaped how I approach any generative stack, including voice.

I have not worked directly on speech-to-text, codecs, or TTS, but the parts of Bland's stack I would want to own are the ones where you have to define what "better" actually means and then measure it honestly. I learn by building, and I would rather take one focused problem across the voice stack and go deep on it.
